description.narrative:
The programme seeks to address the overall problem that CRPD implementation in Fiji is not achieving equitable outcomes for all persons with disabilities in some key areas including inclusive service delivery, equality and non-discrimination, and humanitarian and disaster management. The problem will be addressed through a multi-stakeholder approach that prioritises the meaningful participation and role of Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) through strengthening effectiveness of national monitoring mechanisms (Outcome 2). In addition, building evidence to strengthen the national education system to improve access for children with disabilities in support service and assistive devices and technology needs, with key service delivery duty bearers, the Ministry of Education and special schools and disability service providing organisations, and rights holders (OPDs) (Outcome 2), enhancing outcomes for all persons with disabilities through CRPD compliant national laws and policies, with specific focus on the Employment Relations Act 2007 (Outcome 2), CRPD compliant budgeting (Outcome 1 and Outcome 3), and meaningful participation of OPDs in national humanitarian and disaster management plans (Outcome 3) and the UNCT CCA Framework (Country Implementation Plan) process for Fiji.
The programme will use a multi-stakeholder, multi-sectoral approach in two ways: 1) working through stakeholder coordination mechanisms established during the Inception Phase, namely the OPD sub-working group and Technical Reference Group and broadening this to include other relevant stakeholders across government and OPDs and 2) working through existing multi-sector Advisory Committees of the NCPD. The Joint Programme provides key resources to advance these critical gaps identified during the Situational Analysis and help achieve systemic reforms and enhanced capacity and capability of OPDs to accelerate CRPD implementation and inclusive SDGs in Fiji.
